topic: Stanislav Petrov and the false alarm
hook: In nineteen eighty-three, one man's gut feeling may have prevented a nuclear war.
on_screen_hook: The man who *didn't* start nuclear war

blocks.narration: In nineteen eighty-three, one man's gut feeling may have prevented a nuclear war. Most people have never heard his name.
blocks.visual: Cinematic storybook illustration of a dim Soviet command bunker, glowing screens, dramatic red light

blocks.narration: It was September twenty-sixth, at the height of Cold War tension. Stanislav Petrov was the duty officer at a Soviet early-warning center.
blocks.visual: Illustrated officer in uniform sits before a wall of maps and blinking consoles

blocks.narration: Just after midnight, alarms blared. The satellite system reported a missile launched from the United States, heading toward the Soviet Union.
blocks.visual: A giant illuminated map flashes a red arc across the ocean

blocks.narration: Then it reported more, up to five missiles. Petrov was supposed to report an attack, which could trigger a retaliation.
blocks.visual: Five red arcs appear one after another as sirens strobe

blocks.narration: But something felt wrong. A real first strike would likely involve hundreds of missiles, not five. And the system was new.
blocks.visual: Close-up of Petrov's face lit by red light, thinking, a single drop of sweat

blocks.narration: Ground radar had not confirmed anything. He made a decision under enormous pressure and reported it as a false alarm.
blocks.visual: His hand hovers over a phone, then lifts it calmly as the sirens fade

blocks.narration: He was right. Investigators later found the satellites had mistaken sunlight reflecting off high-altitude clouds for the flash of missile launches.
blocks.visual: Illustrated satellite in orbit as sunlight glints off a bright band of clouds below

blocks.narration: For years he received little recognition, and the story stayed secret. Share this. More people should know his name.
blocks.visual: A quiet snowy Russian town at dawn as the camera slowly pulls back

cta: Share this. More people should know his name.

captions.hook_line: In 1983, one man's gut feeling may have stopped a nuclear war ☢️
captions.body: On September 26, 1983, Soviet duty officer Stanislav Petrov saw the early-warning system report incoming US missiles. He judged it a false alarm and did not pass it up as an attack. It was later traced to sunlight reflecting off clouds.
